token.title: Connect with a Personal Access Token
token.description: Create a token in the DigitalOcean console with read & write scopes. The token is encrypted with AES-256-GCM and stored locally.
token.name: Display name
token.nameHint: Shown in Vatra. Does not need to match your DO team name.
token.tokenHint: From Console → API → Tokens/Keys → Generate New Token. Read+Write recommended.

guide.title: Get a DigitalOcean PAT
guide.description: Droplets, volumes, snapshots, firewalls, floating IPs, VPCs, load balancers, managed databases, Spaces and DOKS all surface in Vatra.

step2.title: Create a new Personal Access Token
step2.body: Navigate to API → Tokens/Keys → Generate New Token. Give it a name (e.g. vmui), set an expiration (90 days is a sensible default), and tick both Read and Write scopes for full lifecycle.
step2.note: If you only want Vatra to observe (no power on/off, no create), uncheck Write.

step3.title: Copy the token (shown once)
step3.body: DigitalOcean displays the token once. Copy it before closing the dialog. If you lose it, generate a new one — old tokens can be revoked from the same page.

step4.title: Pick a default region
step4.body: Choose the region you most often use. You can add more regions later from the account page — Vatra syncs all of them in parallel.

step5.title: Paste the token
step5.body: Switch back to the Personal Access Token tab and paste the value. Vatra verifies it and stores an encrypted copy locally.

token.title: Connect with an API token
token.description: Generate a token in Hetzner Cloud Console → Security → API tokens. Use read & write scope for full lifecycle. The token is encrypted with AES-256-GCM.
token.name: Display name
token.nameHint: Hetzner does not return a friendly project name in the API; pick whatever you want.
token.tokenHint: Console → Security → API Tokens → Generate API Token. Read+Write recommended.

guide.title: Get a Hetzner Cloud API token
guide.description: Hetzner has the cheapest cloud VMs in Europe. ARM cax-* servers start at €3.79/month.

step2.title: Create or select a project
step2.body: Tokens are per project. Either pick an existing project or create a new one (e.g. vmui).

step3.title: Generate an API token
step3.body: Inside the project: Security → API Tokens → Generate API Token. Pick Read & Write for full lifecycle. Copy the 64-character token — shown only once.
step3.note: Tokens never expire automatically. Rotate them by deleting the old one and creating a new one.

step4.title: Pick a default location
step4.body: nbg1 (Nuremberg) and fsn1 (Falkenstein) are the cheapest. ash/hil for North America, sin for Asia.

step5.title: Paste it
step5.body: Switch to the API token tab. Vatra verifies the token by calling /servers and stores an encrypted copy locally.

keys.title: Connect with an API secret key
keys.description: Generate an IAM API key in the Scaleway console. Credentials are encrypted with AES-256-GCM and stored locally.
keys.name: Display name
keys.nameHint: Shown in Vatra — does not need to match your Scaleway project name.
keys.secretKeyHint: UUID-format secret from Console → IAM → API Keys → Create API key.
keys.projectIdHint: From Console → Project dashboard → Project ID button at the top right.
keys.defaultZoneHint: Apple Silicon is only available in Paris. Pick fr-par-1 unless you specifically want a Mac mini M1.

guide.title: Get a Scaleway API key for Apple Silicon
guide.description: Scaleway runs real Mac minis (M1 / M2 / M2 Pro / M4) in Paris with hourly billing after the 24h Apple minimum.

step1.title: Create or sign in to a Scaleway account
step1.body: Open the console and either sign up or sign in.

step2.title: Find your Project ID
step2.body: On the console homepage your Default project is shown. Click it (or any other project) — the top-right shows a Project ID button. Click to copy.

step3.title: Create an API key
step3.body: Go to IAM → API Keys → Create API key. Bearer: your IAM user (yourself). Tick Use this API key for the default project. Copy the Secret key shown once.
step3.note: You only see the secret once — save it to a password manager. If you lose it, just generate another key.

step4.title: Permissions Vatra needs
step4.body: For full functionality grant the IAM user the AppleSiliconFullAccess permission set. For read-only sync, AppleSiliconReadOnly is enough.

step5.title: Paste them in the API key tab
step5.body: Switch back to the API key tab and paste the Secret key and Project ID. Vatra verifies them and stores an encrypted copy locally.

noProfiles.title: No AWS CLI profiles found yet
noProfiles.body: Configure one with either of the commands below, then refresh.

keys.name: Friendly name
keys.nameHint: Just a label shown in Vatra.
keys.accessKeyIdHint: Starts with AKIA (long-term) or ASIA (temporary). From IAM → Users → Security credentials → Create access key.
keys.secretAccessKeyHint: Shown only once at creation. If lost, create a new key pair.
keys.sessionTokenHint: Required only for temporary credentials (AWS SSO / STS / role assumption).

pick.title: Pick your path
pick.description: Two clean ways to connect AWS. Use SSO if your company uses Identity Center; otherwise an IAM user is the quickest.

a.title: A · IAM user (personal)
a.subtitle: Static long-term access keys
a.s1: Best for personal or sandbox accounts.
a.s2: Vatra uses the access key directly.

b.title: B · AWS SSO / Identity Center
b.subtitle: Temporary credentials via browser login
b.s2: You log in via browser; Vatra imports the temporary credentials.
b.s3: About 3 minutes if SSO is already set up.

a.title: Path A — Create an IAM user

step1.title: Sign in to the AWS Console
step1.body: Open <link>IAM → Users</link> (or run the CLI commands below if you already have admin keys).

step2.title: Create a user named vmui-controller
step2.body: The last command prints AccessKeyId and SecretAccessKey. Copy both.

step3.title: Pick how to feed them to Vatra
step3.cliBody: Then go to the AWS CLI profile tab and click Import.
step3.pasteBody: Switch to the Access keys tab and paste them there.

a.note: For tighter security, replace AmazonEC2FullAccess with a custom policy granting only the actions Vatra needs (RunInstances, StartInstances, StopInstances, DescribeInstances, etc.).

b.title: Path B — AWS SSO / IAM Identity Center

step1.title: Configure your SSO profile (one-time)
step1.body: The CLI asks for the start URL (e.g. https://my-org.awsapps.com/start), region, account and role. It opens a browser to authenticate you.

step2.title: Log in (every session)
step2.body: Tokens last about 8h by default. Re-run this when Vatra says credentials expired.

step3.title: Import in Vatra
step3.body: Open the AWS CLI profile tab — your vmui-sso profile appears with an SSO badge. Click Import.

b.note: If you do not have IAM Identity Center set up, your AWS administrator needs to enable it in the management account. Use Path A in the meantime.

kvm.title: WSL2 with /dev/kvm
kvm.body: Should print crw-rw---- 1 root kvm. If missing, CPU virtualisation is off in BIOS or Hyper-V is broken.

setup.title: Run {script}
setup.body: One-time setup: creates {dir}, downloads ISOs, copies OVMF and builds the unattended-install seed.

mac.title: macOS installed (or installing)
mac.body: Connect a VNC client to 127.0.0.1:5900 after starting the VM. First boot needs you to format the virtual disk in Disk Utility and pick Reinstall macOS.

win.title: Drop the Windows 11 ISO at $VMDIR/Win11.iso
win.body: Get the official ISO from microsoft.com/software-download/windows11 (x64 English). Local administrator credentials are baked into autounattend.xml from the values above (or auto-generated when blank).

ubuntu.title: First boot runs cloud-init
ubuntu.body: The setup script downloads the Ubuntu LTS cloud image and seeds cloud-init with the guest credentials above (or auto-generated when blank) plus passwordless sudo. SSH is up within about 60 s; ubuntu-desktop-minimal completes in 5–8 min.
